A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, five figures, two tables, and Appendices A–E, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reading experiments with 54 English and 57 Chinese speakers, model-based information estimates, regression analyses, and appendix results on reading preferences and comprehension.

after.justification: V2 retains these original human experiments, model evaluations, statistical analyses, and supplementary outcomes.

M1.justification: The Bayesian update and entropy-threshold stopping procedure in Equations 1–3, information-estimation methods, and Qwen/TransOCR procedures remain unchanged. The revision changes their theoretical analysis rather than the implemented methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OneStopQA articles and Mandarin translations, English-word and Chinese-character image data, and Full, Upper, and Lower visibility conditions. No language, population, task, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the Bayesian SSIM baseline, zero-shot Qwen2.5, fine-tuned Qwen2.5, and TransOCR. Their participation in Table 1 and the information-gain analyses is unchanged.

E3.justification: Participant counts, randomized visibility conditions, generated training data, held-out evaluation, FPRT measurement, regression controls, and model-training settings are unchanged. No additional evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same recognition examples in Figure 2, word-level and nonlinear analyses in Sections 4.3–4.4, and reading-preference and comprehension analyses in Appendices D–E. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Significance-testing practices and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, including the 20 bootstrap resamples in Section 4.4 and 95% confidence intervals in Figure 4. No new run-count or seed information is disclosed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, Figures 2–5, and Section 4 retain their numerical results and findings. For example, Table 2 still reports Full/Upper/Lower comprehension accuracies of 66/60/56% for Chinese and 81/77/60% for English.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix A remove the unconditional i.i.d. assumption while retaining conditional independence given word identity. Equation 4 changes additive information equalities to upper bounds; Equation 6 becomes an entropy lower bound; Equation 7 changes an approximate sample-count formula to a lower bound. Appendix A revises the derivation using conditioning-reduces-entropy. This substantially changes the central theoretical result and its assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same contributions: information quality measured through mutual information, its relationship to reading effort, and stronger upper/lower asymmetry in English than Chinese. Predictions 1–2 also remain unchanged despite the narrower mathematical result.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 now interprets Equation 7 in terms of minimum required samples. Appendix A revises the sampling rationale around conditional independence and explicitly includes incremental knowledge of word identity. Empirical interpretations remain unchanged; the Limitations section still repeats the former i.i.d. assumption.

D1.justification: Data-generation instructions, access links, and the Qwen and TransOCR implementation details in Appendices B–C remain unchanged, including prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, and inference calculations.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior Bayesian and noisy-channel reading research are unchanged. New thanks to reviewers and a correction credit to Tiago Pimentel do not introduce a cited work or revise research positioning.

P1.justification: Prose revisions are localized to Section 2.2 and Appendix A, alongside an expanded acknowledgments paragraph and a correction-credit footnote. The section sequence and most explanatory text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Limited reflow moves Table 1 from the left to the right column on page 7 and places Table 2 below the Appendix E heading. Appendix A starts on page 12 instead of page 11. Figure and table designs, captions, axes, and legends remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Replacing exact information accumulation and an approximate sample-count formula with bounds makes the theoretical account more defensible, with a corresponding revised derivation in Appendix A. However, the correction is incompletely integrated: the Limitations section still asserts i.i.d. sampling, and the unchanged monotonic reading-time predictions do not follow from a lower bound alone. The revision therefore improves mathematical calibration without fully resolving the connection between theory and interpretation.
